cards.title: Run static-first creative volume instead of VSLs on Meta
cards.summary: Since Meta's Andromeda algorithm rewards sheer creative volume, prioritize a weekly static-ad production cadence over high-production video sales letters.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to allocate your creative budget and team time between video and static ad formats for a Meta campaign.
steps: Accept the source's premise: Andromeda behaves like a 'hungry panda' that needs an absurd volume of fresh creatives before ads fatigue, and producing that volume in video is expensive and slow.

Recognize Facebook can only serve so many video ads per user session, so the algorithm biases toward statics it can show more of per session; the presenter calls this the main reason his cheap native statics beat a VSL that took 2.5 months to produce.
Book one hour every week to produce fresh creatives from your winning offer/product; treat this as the core scaling activity, not a side task.
If you still want video, use proof-of-concept content that already works organically rather than polished productions built from scratch.
Test the format call yourself rather than assuming: the source's claim that statics 'all day of the week' beat video is the presenter's opinion based on his own account.
caveats: The claim that Meta structurally biases toward statics is the presenter's interpretation, not a confirmed platform mechanic.
His account reportedly runs 17 VSLs simultaneously, so his static preference comes from a context of very high existing video volume.
cards.source_name: Learn 97% of Meta Ads in Under 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Use identity triggers in ad copy instead of backend interest targeting
cards.summary: Insert a specific niche, demographic or category keyword directly into your winning ad's headline or body copy so the algorithm finds that buyer pocket for you.
cards.use_when: Preparing ad copy and targeting for a Meta campaign where you want to reach a specific customer segment without manual interest stacking.
steps: Find your best winning ad and identify the 20% of clients that represent 80% of revenue; note the niches they operate in.

Duplicate the winning ad and swap in one of those niches as a keyword: e.g. change '462 leads per week on autopilot' to '462 dental leads,' then repeat with 'lawyer leads,' 'property investment leads,' etc.
Launch the variants and review CTR; the source claims performance improves markedly and that new audience pockets open up that a generic ad would never reach.

Explain the mechanism as the presenter does: it is not a magic word but a category/identity word that feeds the algorithm a signal about who to look for, because the creative now functions as the targeting.
Apply the same idea to demographics: write copy variations for a 25-year-old woman versus a 30-year-old woman so the ad itself carries the targeting context.
caveats: This is one presenter's observed tactic, not a guarantee; validate CTR and cost per lead against your own control ad.
Do not paste niche keywords that misrepresent your offer just to chase a segment.
cards.source_name: Learn 97% of Meta Ads in Under 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Clone your winning ad into hundreds of AI-generated variations
cards.summary: Feed your winning ad to an LLM and generate hundreds of micro-variations targeted to specific demographics, then let CBO pick winners.
cards.use_when: Scaling a proven Meta ad that risks fatiguing, when you need more creative supply from one winning format.
steps: Do not turn off all non-winning ads and ride a single winner to death; the presenter calls that amateur hour because fatigue kills your only asset.

Give the winning ad to an LLM (he names Claude or his own tool Kong; verify current interfaces) with the premise: 'write to 100 people and none of them could tell this was written by a different person.'
Prompt it to rewrite for specific segments, e.g. 'now write this for 25-year-old women' and 'for a 30-year-old woman'; the copy should read almost the same but with details relevant to that person.
Sequence the work: body copy first, then headlines, then the creative itself.
Place all variations into a Campaign Budget Optimization (CBO) campaign and let Meta's AI shift spend toward the best performers.
caveats: The source says CBO cloning has not always been perfect; many ads in the campaign may receive no spend.
LLM output must still fit your offer and compliance requirements; a variant that reads differently to a real buyer defeats the premise.
cards.source_name: Learn 97% of Meta Ads in Under 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Rescue ignored ads with a zombie campaign
cards.summary: Revive high-conviction ads that got zero spend in the main CBO by launching them in an isolated ad set to force delivery.
cards.use_when: After running a CBO clone campaign, when several creatives you believe in recorded zero or near-zero spend.
steps: Collect all ads in the CBO campaign that received no spend but that you have high conviction are genuinely good ads.
Place those dead ads into a separate, isolated ad set — the 'zombie campaign' — and launch it.
The isolated structure forces delivery on ads the algorithm ignored in the primary campaign, letting you extract additional winners.
The source reports typically juicing out another 20% of ads that turn out to be winners; treat that as one operator's example, not a benchmark.
Feed any newly proven winners back into your main scaling structure.
caveats: This is the presenter's tactic and reported result; your extraction rate will vary with account, budget and creative quality.
Only run this for ads you genuinely believe in — it will not turn a weak creative into a winner.
cards.source_name: Learn 97% of Meta Ads in Under 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Make ads that do not look like ads
cards.summary: Produce paid creative that matches natively consumed content in your niche so it does not read as advertising and die on arrival.
cards.use_when: Developing acquisition creative for a Meta or TikTok campaign where polished ad-looking assets are underperforming.
steps: Reject the instinct to make ads 'pop off the feed' and hijack attention; the presenter notes people hate ads and install ad blockers by the hundreds of millions.
Find what content natively performs in your niche. His example: a 46-minute minimally edited YouTube video with millions of organic views is simply run as a paid ad, because it is already proven.

If you lack organic hits, create a burner account: set up fresh TikTok and Instagram accounts, follow all influencers and pages in your niche, and like their content so the platform surfaces the niche's most popular content on your feed.
Use whatever rises to the top of that burner feed as the template for the ads you produce and run.
The source claims this will outperform your current best-performing ad, which is his assertion, not a guaranteed result.
caveats: The performance claim is the presenter's opinion based on his accounts; validate with your own holdout or split test.
Native-looking creative still must comply with platform ad policies and your claims substantiation.
cards.source_name: Learn 97% of Meta Ads in Under 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Test broad targeting against interest stacking with identical creative
cards.summary: Run your best ad with no interest targeting alongside your stacked version and compare CPA after 7 days.
cards.use_when: Reviewing Meta targeting strategy when deciding whether to keep layered interest targeting or move to broad audiences.
steps: Duplicate your best winning creative that currently has interest stacking applied.
Create a version with no interest targeting — just pick a country such as Australia, the US or the UK — and let it run alongside the stacked version.
After 7 days, compare CPAs between the interest-stacked ad and the broad ad.

Treat the underlying principle as the presenter states it: the creative is the targeting now, so more context in the creative lets Meta find the right people, and you should not try to beat Meta's engineers at targeting.
If broad wins, reinvest the time you spent on backend targeting into producing more creative.
caveats: The 7-day window is the source's suggested comparison period; small sample sizes can mislead, so check spend and conversion volume before concluding.
Broad targeting relies on strong creative context; running broad with a thin, generic ad may not replicate the result.
cards.source_name: Learn 97% of Meta Ads in Under 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Write long-form copy to widen Meta's context window
cards.summary: Give the algorithm a large amount of descriptive copy about exactly who you want so it can locate those buyers.
cards.use_when: Writing ad copy for a broad-targeting Meta campaign where the creative must carry the audience definition.
steps: Stop relying on short-form, very basic ad copy; the presenter argues this shrinks the context window Meta has about who you want.
Write long-form copy that explicitly describes the person you are targeting — their situation, role, and the niche keyword signals from your identity triggers.
Understand the causal chain the source asserts: limited context window for your creative means a limited pool of people Meta can target with it; more context expands the reachable audience.
Pair this with broad targeting settings so the algorithm does the placement work while the copy does the qualification.
Judge results on cost per acquisition, not on how polished the copy looks.
caveats: Long copy is not automatically better; it only helps if it contains genuine, accurate targeting context.
This is one operator's framing of how the algorithm uses creative context; validate against your own account data.
cards.source_name: Learn 97% of Meta Ads in Under 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Match your best ad headline to the landing page headline
cards.summary: Mirror the top-performing ad headline, subheadline and lead-in on your landing page to fix scent and lift conversion rate.
cards.use_when: Optimizing a landing page or PDP after ads are driving clicks but conversion rate and CPA are poor.
steps: Compare where effort goes: the source says most advertisers put 90% into ads and only 10% into landing pages, which causes high bounce when the page does not match what was clicked.

Find your best-performing headline by testing 20, 30 or 40 headline variants within an ad, since Meta exposes headlines to roughly a thousand times the people who click through, giving far more statistically significant data than the landing page.
Take the winner and mirror it on the landing page headline, subheadline and copy lead-in.
The presenter reports a minimum 15–20% conversion-rate increase from this alone; treat that as his observed result, not a benchmark.
Run a standing rule of at least three split tests at any time, mining insights from top ads and applying them to the page.
Immediate action: open your top 3 ads and put their headlines side by side with the page headline; fix any mismatch within 24 hours.
caveats: 15–20% is the presenter's personal reported lift, not a guaranteed outcome.
Message match helps conversion rate but only for traffic that was already qualified by the ad; it will not fix a weak offer.
cards.source_name: Learn 97% of Meta Ads in Under 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Retarget non-buyers with a different offer, not the same one louder
cards.summary: Serve people who did not buy a different product or service offer instead of repeating the same ad.
cards.use_when: Building retargeting campaigns for a store or service business with multiple products, to recapture non-converting traffic.
steps: Accept the premise that the number one reason people do not buy is that the offer or product was not right for them, so re-serving the same ad is futile.
Identify what each visitor clicked on — e.g. they came in for protein powder because that is the product they engaged with.

Retarget that audience with a different offer, e.g. creatine. The source describes protein powder at a 2–3x return and the non-buyer retargeting to creatine at around 6x, and says to trust the tactic rather than expect it to make intuitive sense.
Also use a free high-value content offer as the top-of-funnel; outbound calling every person who downloads it tells you their pains, fears, hopes, dreams and why they did not buy.

Build retargeting first as an objection-handling ad from those non-buyer reasons, then proof/testimonial carousels, then a CBO of best-performing ads for other products retargeted to the same audience.
caveats: The 2–3x vs 6x figures are the presenter's illustrated example, not a promised result.
Outbound calling every lead is appropriate for his service-style business; ecommerce stores without a call operation should adapt the objection-gathering step to surveys or post-purchase feedback.
cards.source_name: Learn 97% of Meta Ads in Under 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Scale against blended ROAS and net free cash flow, not platform ROAS
cards.summary: Evaluate changes in absolute store contribution and cash requirements when higher spend lowers reported ROAS.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to increase Meta ad budget when the presenter's peers hesitate because reported ROAS or cost per lead has worsened.
steps: Do not optimize to platform-level ROAS percentages; the presenter reframes the goal as blended ROAS across the whole business, and more importantly net free cash flow.
Distinguish break-even ROAS, a revenue-to-spend ratio, from allowable CPA, a currency amount per acquisition. Calculate both from the store cost model.

Test budget increases against allowable acquisition cost, available cash, inventory and a predefined loss limit; the source aggressive scaling stance is a hypothesis, not an instruction to spend without a ceiling.
Accept compression: the source gives the example that ROAS may fall from 15x to 5x or 10x to 5x, but the point is the absolute net cash generated by spending $100,000 versus $1,000 per month.
When someone reports ROAS dropping from 15 to 11 or cost per lead rising to $50, ask the reframing question: did you make more money in a 30-day period?
Block three hours a month to personally review the numbers rather than relying only on an analyst or media buyer.
caveats: Blended and net free cash flow require accurate, complete accounting; if COGS, fulfillment and refunds are excluded, a break-even ROAS is wrong.
Scaling to break-even assumes you can tolerate thin or zero profit per acquisition to buy market share; the presenter's opinion on this may not fit a cash-constrained store.
The 40x example is anecdotal.
cards.source_name: Learn 97% of Meta Ads in Under 19 Minutes.docx
